claims.label: HYPOTHESIS — not used in verdict
claims.claim: TSC1 knockdown inhibits mTORC1 signalling (lowering IL-2 mRNA production), but the resulting reduction in protein synthesis feedback relieves translational repression of IL-2 protein, allowing existing mRNA to be translated more efficiently and raising surface IL-2.
claims.distinguishing_experiment: Pulse-chase assay: label newly synthesized IL-2 protein with 35S-methionine for 30 min (pulse), then chase in non-radioactive medium for 2–4 hr in TSC1 KD and control cells. Measure half-life by immunoprecipitation and scintillation counting. If IL-2 protein half-life is substantially extended in TSC1 KD (supporting hypothesis 2), the mRNA–protein discordance is driven by stabilization. If half-life is similar but newly synthesized IL-2 accumulates faster during the pulse phase (supporting hypothesis 1), the discordance is driven by translational efficiency relief.

citation.title: TSC2 is phosphorylated and inhibited by Akt and suppresses mTOR signalling.
